44.0.s.en: 1. Blessing upon the godly, the famous heroes of faith

44.0.0.en: 1 Let us praise the noble men, our fathers from whom we were born. 2 In them the Lord created much glory, and displayed His greatness from the ages. 3 They were men of authority in their kingdoms, men of name and might, counselors in their discernment, speaking prophecies, 4 leaders of the people by their counsels, and by the understanding of the books of their nation. 5 They embodied in their instruction words of wisdom, and searched into the melodies of song, and recited the poems of the writing. 6 Men of wealth and power, doing peace in their houses. 7 All those obtained glory in their generations, and their days were days of boasting. 8 Some of them left behind a name that tells of their praises. 9 And some have no memorial, and perished as though they had never been, and were born as though they had not been born, they and their sons after them. 10 But those were men of mercy, and their righteousness is not forgotten. 11 The good inheritance continues with their posterity, and their descendants abide in the promises. 12 Their seed and their sons stand firm for their sake. 13 Their seed continues forever, and their glory is not blotted out. 14 Their bodies were buried in peace, and their names live through all generations. 15 The peoples tell of their wisdom, and the congregation declares their praise.

44.0.1.en: Come now, let us praise the honored men and our fathers [1]; Ben Sira honors the men of faith in the Old Testament, and he bears the same spirit as that found in (Heb 11).

44.1.0.en: The Lord established His great glory, and His greatness from of old, through them [2].

44.1.1.en: Ben Sira takes pride in the glory that God gave to the believers, so that they became glorified, and God was glorified by His work with them.

44.1.2.en: There were those who reigned in their kingdoms, and men who were famous for their power.

44.2.0.en: They offered counsel by their understanding, and proclaimed prophecies [3].

44.2.1.en: He began his discourse by declaring the glory of God without mentioning names, to affirm that He who was glorified in the great men of old is glorified to this day in His believers, and will also be glorified in the generations to come.

44.2.2.en: Ben Sira did not define a particular form for the great ones, but wishes to affirm that the beauty of the holy congregation is that each person works with the talent given to him according to his gifts and abilities. Therefore he spoke of various categories:

44.2.3.en: a. Kings and rulers with authority [2].

44.2.4.en: b. Nobles and leaders with power [3].

44.2.6.en: d. Prophets who received the spirit of prophecy [3].

44.3.0.en: e. Leaders of the people, each in his specialty [4].

44.3.1.en: f. Teachers gifted in the ability to teach [4].

44.4.0.en: g. Artists in melodies and music [5].

44.4.1.en: h. Writers gifted in composing melodies and music [5].

44.5.0.en: i. Rich men generous in giving [6].

44.5.1.en: j. Men of peace gifted in spreading peace between the leaders and the people [6].

44.5.2.en: And there were leaders of the people by their counsels, and by their understanding of the teaching of the people, wise in their words of instruction [4].

44.5.3.en: There were those who composed musical melodies, and recorded poetic writings [5].

44.5.4.en: Rich men with power, living in peace in their dwellings [6].

44.6.0.en: All those obtained glory in their generation, and were a source of pride in their days [7].

44.6.1.en: Ben Sira did not distinguish between one category and another, but sees all the preceding categories marked by obtaining glory, and the holy congregation takes pride in them.

44.7.0.en: Some of them left behind a name that makes people tell of their praises [8].

44.7.1.en: God allows certain faithful and successful names to be brought out, whom the people praise, in order to urge the coming generations to faithfulness and work.

44.8.0.en: And some of them no one remembers; they perished as though they had never been, and died as though they had not been born, and so their sons after them [9].

44.9.0.en: Yet they were men of mercy, and their righteousness lives with the Lord [10].

44.9.1.en: We should not wonder if we see some faithful, sincere and successful men who are no longer remembered, as though they had never been, although they were men of mercy and performed works of righteousness in the Lord. This does not mean that they have been wronged, for what occupies God's mind is that they enjoy the eternal glories. In this there is no difference between one whom men glorify because he walks in the Lord with strength, and one whom history ignores as though he had never existed, for all will be gathered in the great day of the Lord as one heavenly bride.

44.10.0.en: The good that they did continues with their posterity and their children's children [11].

44.11.0.en: Their posterity remains (faithful) to the covenants, and their children likewise on account of them [12].

44.11.1.en: What Ben Sira affirms is that those whom history ignored, and whose portion is in the heavenly places, are not deprived of a holy offspring and grandchildren who are glorified in the Lord. These children and grandchildren are not according to the flesh, but by the Spirit.

44.12.0.en: Their posterity continues forever, and their glory is not blotted out [13].

44.13.0.en: Their bodies were buried in peace, and their names live through all generations [14].

44.14.0.en: The peoples tell of their wisdom, and the congregation declares their praise [15].

44.14.1.en: Ben Sira concluded the introduction "God's men glorify God" with the affirmation that those who receive honor even after their death, and those who do not receive honor, all together as men of God have died, but their story is recorded in the Book of Life, and God is glorified in them through their children and disciples. With this spiritual thought no kind of jealousy or envy will creep in among the people of God, neither in this world nor in the age to come.

44.15.0.en: 16 Enoch pleased the Lord and was translated, and he will call the generations to repentance.

44.15.1.en: Enoch pleased the Lord, and was translated, as an example of repentance for all generations [16].

44.15.2.en: The first example of the famous ones, or of the heroes in the Lord, is Enoch, and he came in the list of the Apostle Paul as the second of the famous (Heb 11:5-6). Jude described him as "the seventh from Adam" (Jude 14).

44.15.3.en: All that is recorded of him in (Gen 5:24) is that he walked with God, and the Lord took him to Himself. He is regarded as the object of God's delight, for he became a lesson to all generations, urging many to a life of repentance in the positive sense, which is meeting with God and walking with Him. He was qualified to become acquainted with heaven, indeed to depart to it.

44.15.4.en: The expression "Enoch pleased the Lord" here means that he was the object of His delight. He became a model of the repentance of the generations; therefore Sirach began with him the list of heroes. This repentance is the beginning of the process of seeking God. He pleased the Lord to the degree that He took him from the earth, and so he clung to Him completely. Enoch was not a Jew, for he lived before Noah and did not receive the covenant with God through Abraham. Rather, he pleased the Lord by keeping the tradition that humanity had received from Adam and Abel.

44.15.5.en: All that Enoch knew about the Lord is that He exists, and he strove to seek Him (Heb 11:6). He believed in God through his little knowledge of Him, and made this knowledge the foundation of his life. If the Book of Sirach is the book of faithful friendship, then God delighted in Enoch as a friend of His, and took him to Himself to be with Him!

44.15.6.en: v Hardly did Enoch feel death at any time within him, and when he was translated to the Lord he let (death) go from his soul, himself. He drove it out by repentance... Rightly it is said that God translated him that he should not see death, since he was no longer susceptible to death, but drove it out and it fled[3].

44.15.7.en: Origen v Enoch remained in a lofty and divine beauty, and purified his soul with holiness and purity.

44.15.8.en: And he excelled in a radiant, pure way of life, and pleased God with thoughts full of love.

44.15.9.en: He was brought up with chaste and pure thoughts, and lived in purity without care or anger.

44.15.10.en: And he dwelt in the wilderness without worldly movements, and pleased God three hundred years while he was looking upon Him.

44.15.11.en: He never found in him a fault, in his sleep or in his wakefulness, nor a slack thought inclined to the world.

44.15.12.en: He continued looking to the Lord every day for three hundred years, and remained in His beauty, and was not stained with defects[4].

44.16.0.en: 17 Noah was found perfect and righteous, and in him was reconciliation in the time of wrath. 18 Therefore a remnant was left on the earth, when the flood came, 19 and covenants were made with him, that all flesh should not be destroyed by the flood.

44.16.1.en: The second example is Noah, whom he called perfect teleios and righteous dekaios [17]. St. Peter said of him that he was a preacher of righteousness dikaiosyne (2 Pet 2:5). Ben Sira did not mention his fall into drunkenness, but brought out that he was found perfect and righteous, and because of him he and his wife and his sons and his sons' wives obtained salvation from the flood, and the eight in the ark became a symbol of the believers in the Church of the New Testament (1 Pet 3:20-21). God made a covenant with Adam, promising him the salvation that the incarnate Word of God, the second Adam, would offer, then Noah received a covenant with God after the flood on behalf of mankind. And the covenant was renewed with the four patriarchs: Noah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (Gen 9:9; 17:9; 26:3-5; 28:13-15).

44.16.2.en: Noah was found perfect and was righteous in the time of wrath, when he became a means of reconciliation[5], and because of him a remnant was left on the earth when the flood came [17].

44.16.3.en: By his righteous life Noah became an object of propitiation for the whole human race. God proclaimed His mercy upon mankind in the form of a covenant between God and men, and declared that He would not destroy the human race with a flood.

44.17.0.en: Everlasting covenants were made with him, so that all flesh would not be blotted out again by a flood [18].

44.17.1.en: Ben Sira brought out that one of the marks of the heroic men of faith is that they enter into a covenant with the Lord, and as for Noah, he entered into "everlasting covenants" [18]. He mentioned the word "covenant" in the plural, perhaps because of the repetition of God's covenant in the Book of Genesis (16:18; 9:9-13, 16-17).

44.17.2.en: v Noah also arose and saw the iniquity of the wicked generation, and wove righteousness and put it on bodily.

44.17.3.en: He armed himself with uprightness and meekness, lest sin stain his body should it meet him.

44.17.4.en: He saw how fornication multiplied among the sons of his generation, so he set virginity in array against it to overcome it by it.

44.17.5.en: He found that everyone had corrupted his way with defiled fornication, so the distinguished one was afraid to approach marriage.

44.17.6.en: He found that nature had slipped and fallen from what was due, so he arose to stand firm in virginity, rising above nature.

44.17.7.en: He kept away from marriage five hundred years, because he found that fornication was among the married[6].

44.17.8.en: He remained in the rank of virginity five hundred years, then married to beget for a purpose.

44.17.9.en: He alone was good, and by his righteousness he comforted the earth, and after the whole world was ruined he made it inhabited through him.

44.17.10.en: He distinguished the sacrifices, and set up an altar with whole burnt offerings, and became in his generation the (holy) "remnant" for the world that perished[7].

44.18.s.en: 4. Abraham, Isaac and Jacob glorify God

44.18.0.en: 20 Abraham was a great father of many nations, and no one was found like him in glory. He kept the law of the Most High, and He made a covenant with him, 21 and established the covenant in his flesh, and when tested he was found faithful. 22 Therefore He swore to him that the nations would be blessed in his seed, and that He would multiply his seed as the dust of the earth, 23 and exalt his descendants as the stars, and cause them to inherit from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth. 24 And likewise He placed in Isaac, for the sake of Abraham his father, 25 the blessing of all men and the covenant, then confirmed them upon the head of Jacob. 26 He favored him with His blessings and gave him the inheritance. He distinguished his portions, and divided them among the twelve tribes. 27 And He raised up from him a man of mercy, who found favor before all flesh.

44.18.1.en: Abraham: regarding Abraham's connection with the Law, the Book of Genesis was concerned with the covenant or compact with God concerning circumcision. Here, however, Sirach brought out the following: 1. Abraham became the icon of the Father, since he enjoyed spiritual fatherhood, not for his family only, nor for one people, but for many nations [19]. 2. There is none like him among men in glory [19], so that reclining in his bosom was counted as reclining in the Kingdom of God (Lk 16:22). This is God's delight, that the heart of the believer be enlarged with love for many peoples. 3. Abraham lived before Moses, the receiver of the law, by about 400 years, yet it is said of him that he kept the law of the Most High [20]. As though the Law were older than the written Law that Moses received. 4. Abraham entered into a covenant with the Most High [20]. 5. God promised to bless Abraham's seed and to multiply it as the dust of the earth, and exalt it as the stars of heaven, and give them an inheritance from sea to sea [21].

44.18.2.en: Abraham was a great father of many nations, and no one was found like him in glory [19].

44.18.3.en: While Noah had his effect upon the remnant that is on the earth [17], Abraham receives a promise of his great fatherhood of many nations [19]. Both promises were fulfilled, to Noah and to Abraham. For the Church is truly a holy remnant that remains for the Lord, and at the same time embraces all the nations, peoples and tongues.

44.18.4.en: Ben Sira mentioned the three heroes: Enoch, then Noah, then Abraham.

44.18.5.en: The first represents God's establishing a personal covenant with the believer, the second the establishing of a covenant on the level of the family (Noah and his household), and the third on the ecumenical level.

44.18.6.en: Thus the Church began on the level of the individual like Enoch, and grew to include the family, and when the Savior of the world came the doors of the Church were opened to all the nations, peoples and tongues.

44.18.7.en: He kept the law of the Most High, who made a covenant with him.

44.18.8.en: He made a covenant in his flesh, and when tested he was found faithful [20].

44.18.9.en: Abraham enjoyed an honor that no one like him enjoyed (44:19), because: 1. He kept the law of the Most High. 2. He entered into a covenant with God, and He confirmed it in his flesh (circumcision). 3. He succeeded in the test of faith (the sacrifice of Isaac his son). Ben Sira spoke of the testing of Abraham [20], and that not in the covenant recorded in (Gen 15:18), but the one recorded in (Gen 17).

44.19.0.en: Therefore He (the Lord) confirmed to him by an oath that in his seed the nations would be blessed, and that He would multiply him as the dust, and exalt his descendants like the stars in number, and cause them to inherit from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth [21].

44.19.1.en: The river here means the river Euphrates.

44.19.2.en: v Abraham arose, a lover of truth and a good servant, and he also formed in his time the front of faith.

44.19.3.en: He left his country and went out after the Lord as He called him, and left his kindred to draw near to God.

44.19.4.en: He walked in the land like an emigrant and did not grow weary, because another world was pictured before him to which to move.

44.19.5.en: He was kindled with love for the Lord as with fire, and with it burned up all the enticements found in the world.

44.19.6.en: He bound his only son on the altar to become a sacrifice, and thrust the spear of the compassions of his bowels to slay him for the Lord.

44.19.7.en: He was tried by the fire and the knife, and proved whether he loved more his children or God.

44.19.8.en: The proof of his love was his binding of his only son...

44.19.9.en: His wife was plundered, his country far off, and his son bound, and since he loved the Lord he did not suffer in all these things[8].

44.19.10.en: St. Jacob of Serugh Isaac was God's gift to Abraham; through him he enjoyed the divine promises of his father.

44.20.0.en: Likewise He established the same covenant with Isaac, for the sake of Abraham his father [22].

44.20.1.en: What occupied Ben Sira in the life of Isaac is that he enjoyed the covenant for the sake of Abraham. This is what he inherited from his father.

44.20.2.en: The blessing rested upon the head of Jacob, who was called "Israel." Although he was younger than Esau he received the inheritance in his seed, as his twelve sons became the fathers of the twelve tribes.

44.20.3.en: The blessing of all men and the covenant that He established remain upon the head of Jacob.

44.21.0.en: He confirmed to him His blessings, and gave him an inheritance, and divided his portions among the twelve tribes [23].

44.21.1.en: What Ben Sira affirms is that Abraham enjoyed the divine covenant, and passed it on to Isaac, then his son Jacob, and the promise was fulfilled in the Church of the Old Testament through the twelve tribes. What occupied Ben Sira in his choice of the heroes was that they serve the people of God, the possessor of the divine promises. Therefore he did not mention in the personality of Jacob, so rich in events, anything except the covenant that God established with him, and what all men enjoyed [23]. As for Joseph, to whom the Book of Genesis devoted a number of chapters, Ben Sira spoke of him in only one phrase, as a helper of his people (49:15).

44.21.2.en: v Isaac also arose and was brought up in beauty, and trained himself in divine thoughts.

44.21.3.en: He filled his soul with faith and humility, and was armed with righteousness and uprightness.

44.21.4.en: He hated strife, and lost his possessions and was not angry, and loved safety while being quiet and virtuous in his works[9].

44.21.5.en: St. Jacob of Serugh v A person can discover through deep reasoning that patience is the foundation of the virtues.

44.22.0.en: By patience Abraham became the father of the nations [24] (Gen 17:5; Rom 4:17), and the friend of God (Jas 2:23).

44.22.1.en: By patience Isaac, after the likeness of the only Son, became a sacrifice (Gen 22:2).

44.22.2.en: And by patience also Jacob carried a staff as a cross (Gen 32:10; Heb 11:21); and he who fled (Gen 27:34), patience made him return full of riches (Gen 32:22-23).

44.22.3.en: By such patience Job struggled and raised the banner of victory, although his adversaries were many and powerful. And although he was completely naked, he appeared as an armed man, fearful before his wrestlers. Job found himself cast down on the ground, and those who wished to create obstacles (the demons) were roaming around him in the air (Eph 2:2). Those who reviled him put on purple, but he put on sores. But the powers of the heavens counted him radiant...

44.22.4.en: The poor glorify him; the rich serve him, and all generations fixed their eyes upon Job as a reflection of righteousness.

44.22.5.en: What need is there of much talk about him? Do you wish to learn the power of the patience that was in Job?

44.22.6.en: There were three friends who reviled him; they were healthy in body, full of vitality because of the overflow of their temporal blessings. And when they grew weary of speaking each of them rested in turn. But as for Job, he alone had his body covered with sores, grieved in soul. By his endurance he overcame these strong men, and by his patience he quieted the fiery, babbling chatter of those who insulted him, relying vainly on their chatter.

44.22.7.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem Inspired by Sirach 44

44.23.s.en: Show me the glory of Your heavenly bride

44.23.0.en: v Grant me, with the heavenly orders, to await the day of Your coming.

44.23.1.en: I see all great and strong, because they are faithful in the truth.

44.23.2.en: There are no longer kings and rulers, counselors and teachers, rich men and nobles, musicians and composers.

44.23.3.en: All have become kings belonging to You, O King of kings. All are musicians ascribed to You, O Source of joy.

44.23.4.en: Billions whom history forgot, and behold they are engraved on Your palm.

44.23.5.en: Many of whom no one knew any offspring, and behold they enter the Kingdom and with them children without number!

44.23.6.en: Many whom we thought to be children of the devil, and behold at the last moments they renounced their evil father and received You as their heavenly Father, and became heirs of the eternal Kingdom.
